ev.q: Among 243 treated patients reporting information about adverse events, 91.4% (222 of 243) experienced at least one adverse event.
The percentage of patients with at least one adverse event classified as severe was higher among patients aged >50 years (31.8%) than among those aged 18–50 years (18.1%; odds ratio = 2.1; p = 0.06).
Among those 1,042 events, 680 (65.3%) were described as mild, 254 (24.4%) as moderate, and 108 (10.4%) as severe.
The percentage of females and males reporting severe adverse events was similar (22.0% and 17.4%, respectively; p = 0.48).
The state with the highest number of patients for whom drug was released was California (115; 34.2%) followed by New York (29; 8.6%)
There was no statistically significant difference between the percentage of females and males reporting adverse events (93.6% and 88.2%, respectively; p = 0.17).
The percentage of patients with at least one adverse event classified as severe was higher among patients aged >50 years (31.8%) than among those aged 18–50 years (18.1%; odds ratio = 2.1; p = 0.06).
Patient characteristics and reported adverse events were recorded for the purpose of drug release under the CDC program.
The prevalence of patient characteristics, reported adverse events, and severity of adverse events are reported.

methods_quotes.q: Fisher’s exact test was used to assess statistical significance (p<0.05).
The prevalence of patient characteristics, reported adverse events, and severity of adverse events are reported.
If multiple releases of the drug were for treatment of the same patient, the associated data were combined.
